objects.definition: typedef struct mpv_handle mpv_handle;
objects.description: Opaque client context handle used to control an mpv instance via the client API. Lifetime is managed by the mpv_* creation/destruction functions; the struct is incomplete/opaque here.

objects.definition:
typedef enum mpv_error {
    MPV_ERROR_SUCCESS           = 0,
    MPV_ERROR_EVENT_QUEUE_FULL  = -1,
    MPV_ERROR_NOMEM             = -2,
    MPV_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED     = -3,
    MPV_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER = -4,
    MPV_ERROR_OPTION_NOT_FOUND  = -5,
    MPV_ERROR_OPTION_FORMAT     = -6,
    MPV_ERROR_OPTION_ERROR      = -7,
    MPV_ERROR_PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND = -8,
    MPV_ERROR_PROPERTY_FORMAT   = -9,
    MPV_ERROR_PROPERTY_UNAVAILABLE = -10,
    MPV_ERROR_PROPERTY_ERROR    = -11,
    MPV_ERROR_COMMAND           = -12,
    MPV_ERROR_LOADING_FAILED    = -13,
    MPV_ERROR_AO_INIT_FAILED    = -14,
    MPV_ERROR_VO_INIT_FAILED    = -15,
    MPV_ERROR_NOTHING_TO_PLAY   = -16,
    MPV_ERROR_UNKNOWN_FORMAT    = -17,
    MPV_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED       = -18,
    MPV_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED   = -19,
    MPV_ERROR_GENERIC           = -20
} mpv_error;
objects.description: Enumeration of libmpv API error codes. Non-negative values indicate success; negative enum constants indicate specific failure reasons.

objects.definition:
typedef enum mpv_format {
    MPV_FORMAT_NONE             = 0,
    MPV_FORMAT_STRING           = 1,
    MPV_FORMAT_OSD_STRING       = 2,
    MPV_FORMAT_FLAG             = 3,
    MPV_FORMAT_INT64            = 4,
    MPV_FORMAT_DOUBLE           = 5,
    MPV_FORMAT_NODE             = 6,
    MPV_FORMAT_NODE_ARRAY       = 7,
    MPV_FORMAT_NODE_MAP         = 8,
    MPV_FORMAT_BYTE_ARRAY       = 9
} mpv_format;
objects.description: Specifies the data representation used when getting/setting properties and options, and within mpv_node values.
Tagged union container used to pass structured/variant data between the API and user code (properties, command args/results). Free contents set by the API with mpv_free_node_contents().
List type used within mpv_node for arrays (values only) and maps (parallel keys/values).
Raw byte buffer wrapper used via MPV_FORMAT_BYTE_ARRAY inside mpv_node.

objects.definition:
typedef enum mpv_event_id {
    MPV_EVENT_NONE              = 0,
    MPV_EVENT_SHUTDOWN          = 1,
    MPV_EVENT_LOG_MESSAGE       = 2,
    MPV_EVENT_GET_PROPERTY_REPLY = 3,
    MPV_EVENT_SET_PROPERTY_REPLY = 4,
    MPV_EVENT_COMMAND_REPLY     = 5,
    MPV_EVENT_START_FILE        = 6,
    MPV_EVENT_END_FILE          = 7,
    MPV_EVENT_FILE_LOADED       = 8,
#if MPV_ENABLE_DEPRECATED
    MPV_EVENT_IDLE              = 11,
    MPV_EVENT_TICK              = 14,
#endif
    MPV_EVENT_CLIENT_MESSAGE    = 16,
    MPV_EVENT_VIDEO_RECONFIG    = 17,
    MPV_EVENT_AUDIO_RECONFIG    = 18,
    MPV_EVENT_SEEK              = 20,
    MPV_EVENT_PLAYBACK_RESTART  = 21,
    MPV_EVENT_PROPERTY_CHANGE   = 22,
    MPV_EVENT_QUEUE_OVERFLOW    = 24,
    MPV_EVENT_HOOK              = 25,
} mpv_event_id;
objects.description: Enumeration of all event kinds returned by mpv_wait_event().
Payload for MPV_EVENT_GET_PROPERTY_REPLY and MPV_EVENT_PROPERTY_CHANGE, describing the property name, its format, and a pointer to retrieved data.
Numeric log severity levels used by the logging subsystem and mpv_event_log_message.
Payload for MPV_EVENT_LOG_MESSAGE containing module prefix, textual level, message text, and numeric log level.
Reasons reported with MPV_EVENT_END_FILE indicating why playback of an entry ended.
Payload for MPV_EVENT_START_FILE; provides the playlist entry ID being loaded.
Payload for MPV_EVENT_END_FILE; communicates termination reason, optional error code, related playlist IDs, and inserted playlist range info.
Payload for MPV_EVENT_CLIENT_MESSAGE; carries an argument vector provided by the sender of script-message.
Payload for MPV_EVENT_HOOK; contains the hook name and an ID required to continue the hook via mpv_hook_continue().
Payload for MPV_EVENT_COMMAND_REPLY; contains structured result data of a command on success.
The event object returned by mpv_wait_event(), carrying the event kind, status/error, request correlation ID, and a pointer to a type-specific payload struct.

objects.definition: typedef struct mpv_render_context mpv_render_context;
objects.description: Opaque render context handle used by the mpv render API. It represents the renderer instance associated with an mpv core. Must be created with mpv_render_context_create() and freed with mpv_render_context_free() before the mpv core is destroyed.

objects.definition:
typedef enum mpv_render_param_type {
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_INVALID = 0,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_API_TYPE = 1,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_OPENGL_INIT_PARAMS = 2,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_OPENGL_FBO = 3,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_FLIP_Y = 4,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_DEPTH = 5,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_ICC_PROFILE = 6,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_AMBIENT_LIGHT = 7,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_X11_DISPLAY = 8,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_WL_DISPLAY = 9,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_ADVANCED_CONTROL = 10,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_NEXT_FRAME_INFO = 11,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_BLOCK_FOR_TARGET_TIME = 12,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SKIP_RENDERING = 13,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_DRM_DISPLAY = 14,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_DRM_DRAW_SURFACE_SIZE = 15,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_DRM_DISPLAY_V2 = 16,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SW_SIZE = 17,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SW_FORMAT = 18,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SW_STRIDE = 19,
    MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SW_POINTER = 20,
} mpv_render_param_type;
objects.description: Enumeration of parameter kinds used with mpv_render_param in creation, rendering, and control of the render context.

Key/value parameter item passed as arrays to various mpv_render_* functions. type selects the meaning, data points to the corresponding value object and is only required to be valid for the duration of the call.
Bit flags describing properties of the next frame to render, used inside mpv_render_frame_info.flags.
Information about the next video frame to render, including bit flags and an absolute display time in microseconds as returned by mpv_get_time_us(). Retrieved via MPV_RENDER_PARAM_NEXT_FRAME_INFO.
Bit flags returned by mpv_render_context_update() indicating what actions are required next. Currently only MPV_RENDER_UPDATE_FRAME.

objects.definition: typedef void (*mpv_render_update_fn)(void *cb_ctx);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the render update callback invoked to signal that a new frame should be rendered or a redraw is needed. The callback must not call mpv APIs.
Initialization parameters for the OpenGL backend of mpv’s render API. Supplies a callback to resolve GL function pointers for the active context and an opaque context value passed to that resolver.
Describes the OpenGL framebuffer object (or default framebuffer) to which mpv should render: FBO name (or 0 for default), dimensions, and optional internal format hint.
Deprecated DRM parameters for OpenGL interop. Carries DRM device/file descriptors and associated KMS objects, plus a pointer to the active atomic request used by the render loop.
Specifies the pixel size of the DRM draw surface (OSD plane) for the OpenGL backend.
Updated DRM parameters for OpenGL interop. Provides DRM/KMS identifiers and an atomic request pointer for the active render loop, plus an optional DRM render-node FD for VAAPI interop.

objects.definition: typedef int64_t (*mpv_stream_cb_read_fn)(void *cookie, char *buf, uint64_t nbytes);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the read callback of a custom mpv stream. Blocking semantics like read(2); returns bytes read, 0 for EOF, -1 for error.

objects.definition: typedef int64_t (*mpv_stream_cb_seek_fn)(void *cookie, int64_t offset);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the seek callback of a custom mpv stream. Return new absolute offset, or MPV_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED/MPV_ERROR_GENERIC on failure. May be NULL when embedded in mpv_stream_cb_info.

objects.definition: typedef int64_t (*mpv_stream_cb_size_fn)(void *cookie);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the size callback of a custom mpv stream. Return stream size in bytes or MPV_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED. May be NULL when embedded in mpv_stream_cb_info.

objects.definition: typedef void (*mpv_stream_cb_close_fn)(void *cookie);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the close callback of a custom mpv stream. Called by libmpv to finalize and release the cookie/resources.

objects.definition: typedef void (*mpv_stream_cb_cancel_fn)(void *cookie);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a cancel callback to interrupt ongoing or future read/seek operations. Optional; may be NULL. Available since API 1.106.

Struct filled by the open callback to describe a custom read-only stream instance: an opaque cookie and the function pointers implementing stream operations. read_fn and close_fn are mandatory; others optional/NULL. Cookie is released via close_fn. The struct is only valid during the open callback for setting fields; mpv copies needed data afterward.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*mpv_stream_cb_open_ro_fn)(void *user_data, char *uri,
                                        mpv_stream_cb_info *info);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the protocol open callback that sets up a read-only custom stream. Fills mpv_stream_cb_info (cookie and callbacks). Returns 0 on success or MPV_ERROR_LOADING_FAILED on failure.

functions.name: mpv_client_api_version
functions.description: Returns the MPV_CLIENT_API_VERSION the library was compiled with. Useful for feature checks and compatibility gating at runtime.
requirements: May be called at any time.
No arguments; thread-safe as per general API guarantees.

functions.name: mpv_error_string
functions.description: Maps an mpv_error code to a static, human-readable string. Returns "unknown error" for unknown codes.
requirements: Argument must be an mpv_error (negative for errors, 0 for success).
Returned pointer is static; do not free or modify.

functions.name: mpv_free
functions.description: General deallocator for memory returned by specific libmpv APIs (e.g., mpv_get_property_string). Use only where explicitly documented.
requirements: Call only on pointers documented as libmpv-owned and freed with mpv_free.
Passing NULL is allowed.
Do not call on memory not owned by libmpv (undefined behavior).

functions.name: mpv_client_name
functions.description: Returns the unique name of the given client handle; read-only and valid until the handle is destroyed.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mpv_handle.
Returned pointer must not be freed or modified.
Valid until mpv_handle is destroyed.

functions.name: mpv_client_id
functions.description: Returns a unique, positive, never-reused integer ID for the client handle; can be referenced as "@<id>" in some APIs.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mpv_handle.
IDs are > 0.

functions.name: mpv_create
functions.description: Creates a new mpv instance in pre-initialized state and returns a client handle. Configure options, then call mpv_initialize() before using most APIs.
requirements: LC_NUMERIC must be set to "C" in the process.
On success, caller must eventually destroy with mpv_destroy() or mpv_terminate_destroy().
May return NULL on OOM or invalid LC_NUMERIC state.
Avoid concurrent access on the uninitialized handle.

functions.name: mpv_initialize
functions.description: Initializes a previously created (but uninitialized) mpv instance; required before most operations if created via mpv_create().
requirements: ctx must be a valid mpv_handle from mpv_create().
Must not be called if already running; returns error in that case.

Certain options that are init-time-only should be set before calling (e.g., config, config-dir, input-conf, load-scripts, script, player-operation-mode, input-app-events, and all encoding-mode options).
Check return code < 0 for errors.

functions.name: mpv_destroy
functions.description: Disconnects and destroys the mpv_handle. If last strong reference, core may be destroyed after weak handles receive shutdown and respond.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mpv_handle or a handle previously returned by libmpv APIs.
Do not call other functions concurrently on the same ctx during destruction.
After return, ctx is invalid.

functions.name: mpv_terminate_destroy
functions.description: Terminates the player and all clients, waiting for shutdown. First call on any handle blocks until core destruction; subsequent calls may not block.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mpv_handle.
Not safe to call other functions concurrently on the same ctx.
After return, ctx is invalid.

functions.name: mpv_create_client
functions.description: Creates a new initialized client handle attached to the same core as ctx (or a fresh core if ctx==NULL), with its own event/log/property observation state.
requirements: If ctx != NULL, it must be an initialized handle (mpv_initialize() already called).
If ctx == NULL, behaves like mpv_create() (ignores name).
Name may be NULL; non-alnum/duplicate names are sanitized by libmpv.
Caller must destroy the returned handle when done.

functions.name: mpv_create_weak_client
functions.description: Creates a weak-reference client handle attached to the same core as ctx. If only weak clients remain, the core is destroyed and weak clients get MPV_EVENT_SHUTDOWN.
requirements: Same requirements as mpv_create_client regarding ctx initialization and name handling.
Be aware that destruction of the last non-weak handle blocks until weak handles are destroyed; avoid using solely for refcounting without considering blocking semantics.
Caller must destroy the returned handle when done.

functions.name: mpv_load_config_file
functions.description: Loads and parses a config file, applying options from its default section as if set via mpv_set_option_string().
requirements: filename should be an absolute path; otherwise behavior unspecified.
Returns MPV_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER if file not found; MPV_ERROR_OPTION_ERROR on fatal parse errors; other option set errors are ignored.
ctx must be a valid handle.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: mpv_get_time_ns
functions.description: Returns a monotonically increasing internal real-time clock in nanoseconds with arbitrary start offset; safe at any time.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
May be called from render API threads and even within wakeup callbacks.

functions.name: mpv_get_time_us
functions.description: Same as mpv_get_time_ns(), but returns microseconds.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
Safe from render API threads and callbacks.

functions.name: mpv_free_node_contents
functions.description: Frees any allocations referenced by an mpv_node previously filled by libmpv (e.g., via mpv_get_property). Does not free the node struct itself.
requirements: Call only for nodes set by libmpv (not for user-constructed nodes).
Safe to call if node->format == MPV_FORMAT_NONE (no effect).
After call, node contents become invalid; caller retains ownership of struct.

functions.name: mpv_set_option
functions.signature: int mpv_set_option(mpv_handle *ctx, const char *name, mpv_format format, void *data)
functions.description: Sets an option (primarily pre-initialize; some may be runtime-settable). Semi-deprecated in favor of mpv_set_property for most options.
requirements: ctx must be valid; typically used before mpv_initialize().
name must be an option name without leading "--".
format must match the value type; data must point to the value of the given format.
Check return value for MPV_ERROR_*.
Do not use for properties where property access is preferred unless required by documented inconsistencies.

functions.name: mpv_set_option_string
functions.signature: int mpv_set_option_string(mpv_handle *ctx, const char *name, const char *data)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for mpv_set_option() with MPV_FORMAT_STRING.
requirements: ctx must be valid; commonly before initialization.
name is an option name without leading "--".
data must be a non-NULL UTF-8 string (encoding caveats per platform apply to filenames/options accepting paths).
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: mpv_command
functions.description: Executes an input command with pre-split C-string arguments (NULL-terminated array). No OSD or string expansion by default.
requirements: ctx must be initialized unless command is valid in pre-init context.
args must be a NULL-terminated array; args[0] should be the command name; subsequent entries are arguments.
Check return value for errors.
For complex/typed args use mpv_command_node().

functions.name: mpv_command_node
functions.description: Executes a command using structured arguments (array for positional or map for named). Optionally returns structured result data in result.
requirements: ctx must be valid (usually initialized).
args must be an mpv_node with format MPV_FORMAT_NODE_ARRAY (positional) or MPV_FORMAT_NODE_MAP (named) using command-defined formats.
If result != NULL and call succeeds, caller must free with mpv_free_node_contents(result).
Check return value; result is not set on error.

functions.name: mpv_command_ret
functions.description: Like mpv_command(), but also returns optional command-specific structured result data.
requirements: args: NULL-terminated array of strings.
If result != NULL and call succeeds, free with mpv_free_node_contents(result).
Check return value for errors before using result.

functions.name: mpv_command_string
functions.description: Executes a command line string parsed like input.conf (supports quoting/escaping). OSD and string expansion are enabled by default.
requirements: args must be a non-NULL command string in the expected syntax.
Parsing may be error-prone due to quoting/escaping; check return value.
ctx should be initialized for typical commands.

functions.name: mpv_command_async
functions.signature: int mpv_command_async(mpv_handle *ctx, uint64_t reply_userdata, const char **args)
functions.description: Queues an asynchronous command. Completion is delivered as MPV_EVENT_COMMAND_REPLY; optional result data is in mpv_event_command.result.
requirements: args is a NULL-terminated array of strings like mpv_command().
reply_userdata can be any 64-bit value (including 0); use to correlate replies.
Safe to call from render API threads.
Only returns error if parsing/queuing fails; otherwise expect an event.

functions.name: mpv_command_node_async
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of mpv_command_node(). Completion arrives as MPV_EVENT_COMMAND_REPLY with optional result.
requirements: args must be a valid structured mpv_node as in mpv_command_node().
reply_userdata is echoed in the reply event.
Safe to call from render API threads.
Only returns error if parsing/queuing fails.

functions.name: mpv_abort_async_command
functions.description: Requests abortion of all pending/ongoing async commands matching reply_userdata. Effect and timing depend on the specific command; completion still arrives as usual with killed/partial work info when supported.
requirements: Only affects async requests with matching reply_userdata for this handle.
Not all commands support abort; then it has no effect.
Be mindful of races: effective only after the async call returns and before its completion event is delivered.

functions.name: mpv_set_property
functions.signature: int mpv_set_property(mpv_handle *ctx, const char *name, mpv_format format, void *data)
functions.description: Sets a property or option at runtime (and, since 0.21.0, many options even before initialization). Accepts typed values and may convert when safe.
requirements: name must be a valid property/option name.
format must correspond to data; implicit conversions may occur (e.g., INT64->DOUBLE, STRING parsing).
Before initialization, setting non-option properties yields MPV_ERROR_PROPERTY_UNAVAILABLE.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: mpv_set_property_string
functions.signature: int mpv_set_property_string(mpv_handle *ctx, const char *name, const char *data)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for mpv_set_property() with MPV_FORMAT_STRING.
requirements: name must be valid; data is a non-NULL string.
Check return value for errors.
Encoding/normalization caveats apply for filenames/strings per platform.

functions.name: mpv_del_property
functions.description: Deletes a property, equivalent to command "del [name]".
requirements: name must be a valid property name.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: mpv_set_property_async
functions.signature: int mpv_set_property_async(mpv_handle *ctx, uint64_t reply_userdata, const char *name, mpv_format format, void *data)
functions.description: Asynchronously sets a property. Completion and status are delivered as MPV_EVENT_SET_PROPERTY_REPLY.
requirements: name, format, and data as in mpv_set_property(); the value is copied and not modified by libmpv.
reply_userdata is echoed in the reply event.
Safe to call from render API threads.
Returns error only if sending the request fails; otherwise expect a reply event.

functions.name: mpv_get_property
functions.signature: int mpv_get_property(mpv_handle *ctx, const char *name, mpv_format format, void *data)
functions.description: Reads a property value, converting to requested format when supported. For dynamic allocations (string/node), caller must free appropriately.
requirements: name must be a valid property name.
format specifies the expected output format; pass a pointer to storage matching that format (e.g., char* variable for STRING to receive malloced buffer pointer).
On success with MPV_FORMAT_STRING, free with mpv_free(); with MPV_FORMAT_NODE, free with mpv_free_node_contents().
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: mpv_get_property_string
functions.description: Convenience getter returning the property as a newly allocated string (or NULL on error).
requirements: name must be valid.
On success, free the returned string with mpv_free().
For precise error info, use mpv_get_property().

functions.name: mpv_get_property_osd_string
functions.description: Returns the property formatted for OSD display as a newly allocated string (or NULL on error).
requirements: name must be valid.
Free the returned string with mpv_free() on success.
Do not parse the returned text; it is intended for display.

functions.name: mpv_get_property_async
functions.signature: int mpv_get_property_async(mpv_handle *ctx, uint64_t reply_userdata, const char *name, mpv_format format)
functions.description: Asynchronously reads a property; completion is MPV_EVENT_GET_PROPERTY_REPLY with mpv_event_property containing the value.
requirements: name must be valid; format specifies desired type.
reply_userdata is echoed in the reply event.
Safe to call from render API threads.
Returns error only if sending the request fails.

functions.name: mpv_observe_property
functions.signature: int mpv_observe_property(mpv_handle *mpv, uint64_t reply_userdata, const char *name, mpv_format format)
functions.description: Registers for notifications when a property changes, delivered as MPV_EVENT_PROPERTY_CHANGE. Optionally returns the value with each change.
requirements: mpv must be a valid handle on which events will be received.
name may reference non-existent properties (allowed).
format can be MPV_FORMAT_NONE (no value) or a concrete format; on error/unavailable, event provides MPV_FORMAT_NONE.
Initial change notification is always sent.
Safe to call from render API threads.

functions.name: mpv_unobserve_property
functions.description: Cancels property observations registered with the given reply_userdata.
requirements: registered_reply_userdata must be the same value used in mpv_observe_property().
Safe to call from render API threads.
Returns >=0 as number of removed properties; negative on error.

functions.name: mpv_event_name
functions.description: Returns a static, lowercase hyphenated string name for a given event ID, or NULL for unknown IDs.
requirements: event must be a value from mpv_event_id; unknown values return NULL.
Returned string is static; do not free or modify.

functions.name: mpv_event_to_node
functions.description: Converts an mpv_event into a structured mpv_node (MAP) with fields mirroring mpv_event and associated event data. Caller must free node contents.
requirements: dst must be a valid pointer; contents will be overwritten; free with mpv_free_node_contents(dst) on success.
src must point to a valid mpv_event (not const by signature, but not modified).
Safe to call from render API threads.
Check return for errors (typically MPV_ERROR_NOMEM only).

functions.name: mpv_request_event
functions.signature: int mpv_request_event(mpv_handle *ctx, mpv_event_id event, int enable)
functions.description: Enables or disables delivery of a specific event type to this handle.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
event is a value from mpv_event_id; some events are always enabled/disabled regardless.
enable must be 0 (disable) or 1 (enable).
Safe to call from render API threads.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: mpv_request_log_messages
functions.description: Sets the minimum log level for receiving MPV_EVENT_LOG_MESSAGE events on this handle.
requirements: min_level must be one of: "no", "fatal", "error", "warn", "info", "v", "debug", "trace", or "terminal-default" (since 1.19).
ctx must be valid.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: mpv_wait_event
functions.description: Waits for the next event up to the specified timeout, returning a pointer to an internal mpv_event. Use timeout 0 for polling; negative for infinite wait.
requirements: Only one thread may call this on the same mpv_handle at a time.
Do not write to or free the returned pointer; it remains valid until the next mpv_wait_event() on this handle or handle destruction.
If event queue overflows due to not polling fast enough, events are dropped and async requests may fail with MPV_ERROR_EVENT_QUEUE_FULL.
As long as timeout is 0, safe to call from render API threads.

functions.name: mpv_wakeup
functions.description: Interrupts a thread currently blocked in mpv_wait_event() on this handle, causing it to wake up (often returning MPV_EVENT_NONE, unless other events are queued).
requirements: ctx must be valid.
Safe to call from render API threads.
Next mpv_wait_event() call will return immediately if none was waiting (to avoid lost wakeups).

functions.name: mpv_set_wakeup_callback
functions.description: Registers a callback that is invoked when new events are available, to integrate with external event loops. Callback must be fast, non-blocking, and must not call libmpv APIs.
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear the callback.
Callback may be called from arbitrary foreign threads; must not call any mpv client API, must return normally (no exceptions/longjmp), and must not change thread-local state like FP environment.
Use callback only to signal another thread which then drains events via mpv_wait_event().
Only one wakeup callback can be set per handle.
d is user data passed to the callback.

functions.name: mpv_wait_async_requests
functions.description: Blocks until all outstanding asynchronous requests (e.g., mpv_command_async) on this handle have completed. Also resets the suspend counter if mpv_suspend() was used.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
Do not rely on this to drain the event queue (it does not empty it).

functions.name: mpv_hook_add
functions.signature: int mpv_hook_add(mpv_handle *ctx, uint64_t reply_userdata, const char *name, int priority)
functions.description: Registers a hook handler. When the hook fires, you receive MPV_EVENT_HOOK; you must respond with mpv_hook_continue() to let the player proceed.
requirements: name should be a documented hook name; unknown names simply never fire.
priority orders handlers: lower runs first; equal priorities run in registration order. Use 0 as neutral default.
Only the registering handle receives the hook events.
Safe to assume reentrancy only if documented for the specific hook.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: mpv_hook_continue
functions.description: Resumes the player after handling a MPV_EVENT_HOOK event identified by the provided id.
requirements: id must be the mpv_event_hook.id received for the corresponding MPV_EVENT_HOOK.
Call exactly once per hook event; multiple calls, wrong IDs, or using a different handle are undefined behavior.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: mpv_get_wakeup_pipe
functions.description: [Deprecated] Returns a UNIX file descriptor (read end of a non-blocking pipe) that becomes readable when new events are available, to integrate with poll/select loops. Closed when the handle is destroyed.
requirements: Available only when MPV_ENABLE_DEPRECATED is enabled and not on Windows/MinGW (returns -1 on those).
Caller must read and drain the pipe before calling mpv_wait_event(mpv, 0) in a loop to avoid missed wakeups.
FD is constant per-handle; do not write to it; close is handled by libmpv upon handle destruction.
Prefer mpv_set_wakeup_callback() for new code.

functions.name: mpv_render_context_create
functions.description: Create and initialize a rendering context for mpv using a selected backend (e.g., OpenGL or software). Pass a parameter array describing the API type and required backend-specific init parameters. On success, stores the created context in *res. Use this before playback to allow explicit rendering via the render API, and free it with mpv_render_context_free() when done.
requirements: res must be a valid pointer; on success, *res is set to a new context, on failure it is set to NULL
mpv must reference the target mpv core (the created context will be tied to that core)
params must be an array of mpv_render_param terminated with type == MPV_RENDER_PARAM_INVALID (0)
params must include MPV_RENDER_PARAM_API_TYPE and the backend-specific init parameter(s) (e.g., MPV_RENDER_PARAM_OPENGL_INIT_PARAMS for OpenGL)
If using X11/Wayland params, the provided display handles must remain valid for the lifetime of the mpv_render_context
At most one mpv_render_context can exist per mpv core at a time
Must not be called concurrently with other mpv_render_* functions for the same mpv core
Must not be called from within callbacks set by mpv_set_wakeup_callback() or mpv_render_context_set_update_callback()
If the OpenGL backend is used, the same GL context used to create the mpv_render_context must be current in the calling thread for mpv_render_* calls unless otherwise documented
The context must be freed with mpv_render_context_free() before the mpv core is destroyed (otherwise undefined behavior)

functions.name: mpv_render_context_set_parameter
functions.description: Attempt to change a single renderer parameter at runtime (e.g., set an ICC profile). Supported parameters and mutability depend on the backend and parameter type. Returns success only if the parameter is actually applied.
requirements: ctx must be a valid render context
Only certain mpv_render_param_type values are supported for setting; others return an error
param.data must point to the documented type for the given param.type
Must not be called concurrently with other mpv_render_* functions for the same mpv core
Must not be called from within callbacks set by mpv_set_wakeup_callback() or mpv_render_context_set_update_callback()
If the OpenGL backend is used, the correct OpenGL context must be current in the calling thread

functions.name: mpv_render_context_get_info
functions.description: Retrieve information from the render context for specific query types (e.g., MPV_RENDER_PARAM_NEXT_FRAME_INFO). You pass a param with type set and data pointing to storage; on success the function writes the result into the provided storage.
requirements: ctx must be a valid render context
param.type must be a value that explicitly supports retrieval via this function (e.g., MPV_RENDER_PARAM_NEXT_FRAME_INFO); otherwise returns MPV_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
param.data must point to writable storage of the required type for param.type
Must not be called concurrently with other mpv_render_* functions for the same mpv core
Must not be called from within callbacks set by mpv_set_wakeup_callback() or mpv_render_context_set_update_callback()
If the OpenGL backend is used, the correct OpenGL context must be current in the calling thread

functions.name: mpv_render_context_set_update_callback
functions.description: Register a callback to be notified when a new video frame is available or a redraw is required. Calling this function triggers the callback once immediately. The callback must not call any mpv API and must return normally (no exceptions).
requirements: ctx must be a valid render context
May be called from any thread except from within an update callback itself
The registered callback must not call any mpv API functions
The callback must not exit by throwing exceptions
Calling this function will cause an immediate callback invocation
Must not be called concurrently with other mpv_render_* functions for the same mpv core

functions.name: mpv_render_context_update
functions.description: Process pending render updates after an update callback was raised and return a bitset of mpv_render_update_flag values (e.g., MPV_RENDER_UPDATE_FRAME). When MPV_RENDER_PARAM_ADVANCED_CONTROL is enabled, calling this after each update callback is mandatory and may perform additional setup (like allocating decoder textures).
requirements: ctx must be a valid render context
Call on the render thread after an update callback; do not call from within the update callback itself
If MPV_RENDER_PARAM_ADVANCED_CONTROL is enabled, this must be called after each update callback (calling once after multiple callbacks is acceptable if it couldn’t be called sooner)
If another update callback occurs during or after this call, it must be called again as soon as possible
Must not be called concurrently with other mpv_render_* functions for the same mpv core
If the OpenGL backend is used, the correct OpenGL context must be current in the calling thread

functions.name: mpv_render_context_render
functions.description: Render the next video frame (or redraw the previous frame) to a backend-specific target (e.g., OpenGL FBO or a software buffer). Applies playback options (scaling, panscan, etc.). May block to align presentation time unless timing is disabled. Required params depend on the backend; for software rendering, specific MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SW_* fields are mandatory.
requirements: ctx must be a valid render context
params must be an array of mpv_render_param terminated with type == MPV_RENDER_PARAM_INVALID (0)
Provide backend-specific target parameters (e.g., MPV_RENDER_PARAM_OPENGL_FBO for OpenGL)
Optional transform/timing parameters may be provided (e.g., MPV_RENDER_PARAM_FLIP_Y, MPV_RENDER_PARAM_DEPTH, MPV_RENDER_PARAM_BLOCK_FOR_TARGET_TIME, MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SKIP_RENDERING)

For MPV_RENDER_API_TYPE_SW, the following are mandatory: MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SW_SIZE, MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SW_FORMAT, MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SW_STRIDE, MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SW_POINTER (with the documented alignment and layout semantics)
Must not be called concurrently with other mpv_render_* functions for the same mpv core
Must not be called from within callbacks set by mpv_set_wakeup_callback() or mpv_render_context_set_update_callback()
If the OpenGL backend is used, the correct OpenGL context must be current in the calling thread
If MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SKIP_RENDERING is set, a target surface is not required but the call still counts as rendering a frame and timing rules apply

functions.name: mpv_render_context_report_swap
functions.description: Inform the renderer that a frame flip/swap occurred at the current time. This is optional but can improve timing. Once you start using it, use it consistently for good playback quality.
requirements: ctx must be a valid render context (calls are ignored if no video is initialized)
Using this intermittently can harm playback timing; if used, it should be used consistently
Must not be called concurrently with other mpv_render_* functions for the same mpv core
Must not be called from within callbacks set by mpv_set_wakeup_callback() or mpv_render_context_set_update_callback()
If the OpenGL backend is used, the correct OpenGL context must be current in the calling thread

functions.name: mpv_render_context_free
functions.description: Destroy and free the render context, disabling video if it is still active. Safe to pass NULL (no-op). Must be called before the associated mpv core is destroyed.
requirements: ctx may be NULL (function does nothing) or must be a valid render context pointer
Must be called before the mpv core is destroyed; otherwise undefined behavior
Calling while a VO is using the render context is allowed but will disable video forcefully
Must not be called concurrently with other mpv_render_* functions for the same mpv core
Must not be called from within callbacks set by mpv_set_wakeup_callback() or mpv_render_context_set_update_callback()
On render threads: mpv_render_* functions are only safe for the same mpv_render_context pointer; freeing a different context from the render thread is not safe as per threading notes

functions.name: mpv_stream_cb_add_ro
functions.signature: MPV_EXPORT int mpv_stream_cb_add_ro(mpv_handle *ctx, const char *protocol, void *user_data, mpv_stream_cb_open_ro_fn open_fn);
functions.description: Registers a custom read-only stream protocol with an mpv instance. After registration, opening a URL with the matching protocol prefix (e.g., "foo://...") will invoke the provided open callback, which must fill an mpv_stream_cb_info with the stream’s callbacks and cookie. The registration persists for the lifetime of the mpv core (it can outlive the mpv_handle used to register it) and is removed when the core is terminated. Use this to plug custom data sources into mpv’s demuxing/decoding pipeline. Note: stream callbacks must not invoke libmpv APIs on the same instance/handle to avoid deadlocks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized mpv_handle associated with the mpv core that should own the protocol registration.
protocol must be a valid, non-NULL, NUL-terminated protocol prefix string (e.g., "foo" for "foo://" URIs).
open_fn must be a valid, non-NULL callback of type mpv_stream_cb_open_ro_fn.
The open_fn must set mpv_stream_cb_info.read_fn and mpv_stream_cb_info.close_fn (both are mandatory).
The open_fn may optionally set mpv_stream_cb_info.seek_fn, size_fn, and cancel_fn (if unsupported, leave NULL or return MPV_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED from those callbacks where specified).
The open_fn may set mpv_stream_cb_info.cookie to an opaque value identifying the stream instance; it will be passed to all callbacks and released by close_fn.
The mpv_stream_cb_info passed to open_fn is only valid during the open_fn call; callbacks and cookie pointers cannot be changed later.
open_fn must return 0 on success, or MPV_ERROR_LOADING_FAILED if the given URI cannot be opened.
Stream callbacks must not call libmpv APIs in a way that can deadlock (do not call libmpv APIs on the same mpv_handle/instance from within the callbacks).
Caller must check the return value of mpv_stream_cb_add_ro; if a protocol with the same name is already registered, the function returns MPV_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER and no registration occurs.
This function only supports read-only streams; writing is not supported via this API.
